tests.title: System discovery separates public bootstrap from encrypted capability inputs
tests.description: Reuses the current discovery and encrypted-controlplane unit coverage to prove that browser bootstrap relays are resolved from approved public inputs while encrypted capability remains gated by dedicated encrypted-request relay plus service-pubkey inputs.
preconditions: Canonical public-only and sidecar-first Nostr discovery fixtures are available.
Unit tests can mock the browser auth and system stores.
steps: Resolve browser relay bootstrap inputs from Nostr discovery and confirm `nostr.relays` is ignored for browser bootstrap.
Evaluate encrypted capability against a public-only payload and a payload with encrypted-request relay plus service-pubkey inputs.
tests.expected_result: Public bootstrap succeeds without implying encrypted capability, and encrypted capability becomes available only when dedicated encrypted discovery inputs are present.
data_requirements: One payload with only public browser relay bootstrap fields.
One payload with browser encrypted request relays and service pubkey.
determinism_notes: Pure fixture-driven unit coverage; no live relays or HTTP services required.

tests.title: Representative public signer-first browser flow records accepted OK and completes from public relay events
tests.description: Extend the existing public service-to-deployment smoke to record accepted relay OK responses alongside request/result/read-model traces so the test proves canonical public completion semantics rather than only public request kind usage.
preconditions: A signer-authenticated browser session is mocked by the Playwright harness.
System discovery advertises only public browser relays for the representative flow under test.
steps: Execute the existing create-service and deployment approval journey.
Capture public publish relay URLs, accepted OK responses, correlated result events, and resulting read-model projections.
Assert no encrypted request kind or REST mutation response is treated as canonical completion evidence.
tests.expected_result: The representative public flow publishes only through public relays, requires at least one accepted OK per canonical request, and completes from correlated public result plus read-model events.
mocks: public WebSocket relay harness with OK/EVENT/EOSE support
data_requirements: Stable public request kind set for service create, policy preview, deployment intent, and approval.
Deterministic deployment intent and run projection payloads.
determinism_notes: All relay traffic is injected by the local Playwright harness; no external relays are contacted.
The harness should assert correlation by request id instead of using arbitrary wait thresholds.
tests.failure_reason: Implemented accepted-OK/result/projection trace assertions in the public harness/spec, but targeted Playwright verification is currently blocked by an unrelated Bahia web bootstrap TypeError from concurrent UI/icon changes.

tests.title: Encrypted controlplane transport publishes only 5980 requests and resolves only correlated 7980 results
tests.description: Uses the existing transport unit suite to prove request kind, relay selection, accepted-OK handling, correlated encrypted result filtering, dedupe, and spoof rejection for encrypted browser traffic.
preconditions: Browser auth helpers can sign and encrypt test events.
Encrypted relay URLs and service pubkey are available from mocked Nostr discovery.
steps: Build an encrypted request event for a sensitive browser operation.
Publish the event through the encrypted controlplane client and inspect OK handling.
Inject unrelated, spoofed, duplicate, and correlated encrypted results.
tests.expected_result: Only 5980 encrypted requests are published, only encrypted-request relays are used, and only the correlated service-authored 7980 result resolves the request.
data_requirements: Stable requester pubkey, service pubkey, request event id, and correlated result payload.
determinism_notes: All events are injected synchronously into mocked handlers; no live relays or timers are required for completion.

tests.title: Representative notifications browser flow stays entirely on encrypted request/result relays
tests.description: Reuses the notification encrypted transport smoke as the representative browser proof that a sensitive domain publishes and resolves end to end on encrypted request/result relays only.
preconditions: System discovery advertises both public and encrypted relay inputs.
The browser signer mock exposes NIP-44 encryption helpers.
steps: Load the notifications route.
Create and test a notification channel.
Inspect encrypted relay and operation traces.
tests.expected_result: The browser performs list/create/test notification operations only on the encrypted relay set and never publishes the sensitive payloads to the public relay set.
data_requirements: Stable notification channel form data and encrypted operation names.
determinism_notes: Relay publish and result events are generated entirely inside the Playwright harness.

tests.title: Encrypted browser flows fail closed when capability or signer support is absent
tests.description: Extend the current fail-closed unit coverage so it proves both halves of the AC: missing encrypted discovery inputs and signer/browser modes that do not expose usable NIP-44 encrypt/decrypt helpers. Added explicit signer-without-browser-visible-NIP-44 coverage that rejects before publish/subscribe and proves no public-relay fallback.
preconditions: One test scenario omits encrypted discovery inputs.
One test scenario reports encrypted requests unavailable to route stores.
steps: Evaluate encrypted availability against a public-only Nostr discovery payload.
Call an encrypted route-store operation when encrypted requests are unavailable.
Attempt an encrypted browser operation with a signer mock that lacks usable browser-visible NIP-44 encrypt/decrypt support.
tests.expected_result: Encrypted transport is reported unavailable, no encrypted publish occurs, and no public-relay fallback path is attempted for the sensitive flow in either the missing-discovery or missing-signer-capability scenario.
mocks: signer/auth mock without browser-visible NIP-44 support
data_requirements: Stable public-only Nostr discovery payload.
Deterministic unavailable-capability error text for both discovery-missing and signer-capability-missing cases.
determinism_notes: Coverage is local and synchronous apart from resolved mock promises.

tests.title: Protected browser routes do not require blanket REST compatibility by default
tests.description: Uses the existing route-access suite to prove the default protected-route policy leaves `requiresRestCompatibility` false unless an explicit override is injected.
preconditions: Default route-access configuration is loaded with no E2E compatibility overrides.
steps: Inspect protected prefixes such as `/souls` and `/llm` under the default route-access policy.
Inject an explicit compatibility override and confirm the override path is the only path requiring REST compatibility.
tests.expected_result: Protected routes remain auth-guarded, but blanket REST compatibility is not required by default.
data_requirements: Stable protected route paths and one explicit override path.
determinism_notes: Pure in-memory policy evaluation with no network dependency.

tests.title: Payments page history surface loads through encrypted browser requests only
tests.description: Reuses the encrypted payments store tests to prove the `/payments` payment-history surface requests data through encrypted transport and surfaces encrypted errors without a REST fallback path. This row intentionally covers only the `/payments` surface; the dashboard spend-summary half of AC6 remains tracked separately by TPG-T-008.
preconditions: The payments store is loaded with a mocked encrypted request helper.
steps: Load payment history for a worker.
Inspect the encrypted operation and payload.
Return an encrypted error envelope and verify local error handling.
tests.expected_result: The payments page uses `payments.history` over encrypted transport and does not substitute REST when the encrypted result fails.
data_requirements: Stable worker pubkey, limit, and encrypted payment-history payload.
determinism_notes: Store behavior is exercised with mocked promises only.

tests.title: Dashboard recent-spend summary stops depending on REST payments history
tests.description: Replace the current REST `payments/history` dashboard mocks with an encrypted spend-summary harness or shared encrypted-store path so the dashboard spend card proves the approved encrypted browser transport instead of legacy REST drift.
preconditions: The dashboard exposes a Recent Spend card.
Encrypted browser capability is available in the test harness.
steps: Load the dashboard with deterministic worker and spend fixtures.
Capture all payment-related transport activity and assert no REST `payments/history` request is used as the canonical data source.
Exercise an encrypted partial-failure case for one worker and verify the UI still reflects encrypted-source semantics.
tests.expected_result: The dashboard spend summary is sourced from the approved encrypted transport path and no longer depends on REST `payments/history` for canonical browser behavior.
fixtures: deterministic recent payment fixture per worker
mocks: encrypted request/result relay harness for payment summaries
fetch interceptor asserting zero canonical `payments/history` reads
data_requirements: At least one successful worker payment response and one partial-failure scenario.
Deterministic total and count outputs for the Recent Spend card.
determinism_notes: The test should fail if the page requires REST payment-history mocks, which is the current implementation drift captured by HITL-TRANSPORT_POLICY_GOVERNANCE-002.

tests.title: Approved browser transport slices do not depend on EventSource log streaming
tests.description: Add a transport-policy contract test that enumerates approved browser slices and asserts none of them import or require `streamLogs(...)` / EventSource as approval evidence. The legacy `api-client-retry-and-edges.test.js` coverage remains negative implementation evidence only.
preconditions: Approved browser slices for this feature are enumerated in the contract test.
Legacy EventSource helper coverage remains present for drift visibility.
steps: Resolve module dependencies or exported route helpers for the approved browser transport slices.
Assert no approved slice references `BahiaClient.streamLogs` or constructs EventSource for canonical behavior.
Document legacy SSE coverage as non-approval evidence.
tests.expected_result: Approved browser transport proof does not require EventSource streaming, and legacy SSE helper coverage cannot satisfy the transport-policy contract by itself.
mocks: module import spy or static dependency scan helper
data_requirements: Stable list of approved routes/stores covered by TRANSPORT_POLICY_GOVERNANCE.
determinism_notes: A static dependency assertion is preferred over browser waits so the proof stays deterministic and does not confuse legacy SSE code with approved transport behavior.
tests.failure_reason: Target contract test file `web/tests/unit/transport-policy-contract.test.js` does not exist yet.

tests.title: Operator explicit relay configuration remains limited to explicit pre-acceptance failures
tests.description: Reuses the signer-first operator adoption runtime tests that already prove fallback behavior is explicit, compatibility-only, and forbidden after any relay has accepted the signer-first request.
preconditions: Operator CLI/client tests can construct synthetic pre-acceptance and post-acceptance failures.
steps: Trigger a pre-acceptance signer-first error with fallback enabled.
Trigger a post-acceptance terminal signer-first error under the same fallback configuration.
tests.expected_result: Fallback executes only for the pre-acceptance case and never after an accepted signer-first request.
data_requirements: Stable synthetic `ControlPlaneRequestError` values with request-accepted true and false variants.
determinism_notes: Existing focused Go unit coverage already exercises this behavior without live relay dependencies.

tests.title: Canonical approval evidence uses 596x/597x/598x families while 311xx remains compatibility-only
tests.description: Run a fixed review checklist over the docs and approval-backed test corpus to confirm that 31100–31105 references remain compatibility-only and that primary acceptance proof uses modern public or encrypted request families instead.
preconditions: The current approval-backed public and encrypted test files are identified.
Documentation references for legacy 311xx handling are available.
steps: Inspect canonical transport docs for how 311xx is classified.
Inspect the representative public and encrypted approval-backed tests for request families used as proof.
Record whether any new approval evidence promotes 311xx as a primary transport family.
tests.expected_result: Approved proof relies on 596x/597x/598x request families, and 311xx remains documented and treated as compatibility-only behavior.
data_requirements: Stable set of approval-backed docs and representative test files.
determinism_notes: This review is manual because the current requirement is about classification across docs and proof artifacts, not runtime behavior. If regressions recur, replace this with a doc-lint check.

tests.title: Settings relay visibility is sourced from a service-authored NIP-51 kind 30002 event
tests.description: Add a settings-page regression that seeds a service-authored NIP-51 kind 30002 relay-list event and verifies the operator-facing UI renders that data without relying on raw `systemInfo.nostr.relays` discovery fields. The settings regression now verifies service-authored NIP-51 service relay-list display with raw discovery relays omitted.
preconditions: A service-authored kind 30002 relay-list event is available to the browser in the harness.
The settings page can be loaded without `systemInfo.nostr.relays` populated.
steps: Load settings with Nostr discovery that omits raw `nostr.relays` but includes the standard service identity and browser bootstrap inputs.
Inject a service-authored kind 30002 relay-list event.
Verify the UI shows operator-facing server relay visibility from the kind 30002 event and keeps it distinct from browser bootstrap relay configuration.
tests.expected_result: Operator relay visibility is rendered from the service-authored NIP-51 event and does not regress to raw system discovery fields.
mocks: relay subscription harness capable of serving kind 30002 events
data_requirements: Stable service pubkey and stable ordered relay URL list for operator display.
determinism_notes: This test should be implemented only with deterministic injected relay events; do not query live relays for kind 30002 in CI.

tests.title: Public controlplane bootstrap uses EOSE-bounded catch-up then live subscriptions
tests.description: Reuses the controlplane store tests that prove public relay-backed state bootstraps through `queryUntilEose`, then transitions to a live subscription, and fails closed when relay-read-model capability is absent.
preconditions: A mocked Nostr client exposes `queryUntilEose`, `subscribe`, and connection-state hooks.
steps: Bootstrap the controlplane store from Nostr discovery relays.
Inspect the EOSE-bounded historical query, live subscription setup, and resulting connection state.
Verify failure when relay-read-model capability is not advertised.
tests.expected_result: Public relay-backed bootstrap derives readiness from historical query completion plus live subscription setup, not polling heuristics.
mocks: mock Nostr client with queryUntilEose and subscribe hooks
data_requirements: Stable read-model event kinds and a deterministic service pubkey author.
determinism_notes: Historical and live events are injected directly; no sleeps are required to prove bootstrap semantics.

tests.title: Encrypted request/result completion depends on accepted OK and correlated terminal events
tests.description: Reuses encrypted transport unit coverage to prove that encrypted completion and failure derive from accepted publish responses, subscription events, correlated requester/service tags, and relay-closure handling rather than timeout or polling heuristics.
preconditions: Encrypted transport client and result subscription handlers are mocked.
steps: Publish an encrypted request with both accepted and rejected OK scenarios.
Inject unrelated, spoofed, duplicate, and correlated terminal result events.
Exercise decrypt-failure and relay-close paths.
tests.expected_result: Encrypted completion depends on accepted publish plus correlated terminal result events, and failure paths surface from explicit result/decrypt/relay-close signals rather than arbitrary waits.
mocks: fake encrypted Nostr client subscribe/publish hooks
data_requirements: Stable request id, requester pubkey, service pubkey, and terminal result envelope.
determinism_notes: Completion is driven directly by injected handlers; no polling loop is involved.

tests.title: One authenticated browser session keeps public and encrypted journeys on the shared Bahia relay set
tests.description: Add a dual-transport Playwright proof that, within one authenticated browser session, a representative public service/deployment action and a representative encrypted notification action both complete successfully while staying on their respective relay sets end to end.
preconditions: System discovery advertises both public browser relays and encrypted request relays.
The shared browser auth harness supports both signer-first public requests and encrypted NIP-44 operations.
steps: In one browser session, execute a representative public service/deployment action.
Without resetting the session, execute a representative encrypted notifications action.
Inspect public and encrypted transport traces together and verify neither flow depends on the wrong relay set or REST compatibility overrides.
tests.expected_result: The public journey uses only public relay transport, the sensitive journey uses only encrypted request/result transport, both complete in one session, and the shared discovery contract does not blur the transport boundary.
data_requirements: Stable request ids and relay URLs for both relay sets.
Deterministic public and encrypted domain payloads for the selected representative flows.
determinism_notes: Use the existing local public and encrypted harness patterns; do not rely on `waitForTimeout` or live relay timing to prove separation.
tests.failure_reason: Implemented mixed public-plus-encrypted single-session proof, but targeted Playwright verification is currently blocked by an unrelated Bahia web bootstrap TypeError from concurrent UI/icon changes on the services page.

known_gaps: TPG-T-002: accepted-OK public proof is implemented but Playwright verification is blocked by unrelated concurrent UI bootstrap failure.
TPG-T-009: EventSource exclusion has no dedicated contract test yet.
TPG-T-015: mixed single-session relay-separation proof is implemented but Playwright verification is blocked by unrelated concurrent UI bootstrap failure.

implementation_notes: Low implementation effort: TPG-T-001, TPG-T-003, TPG-T-004, TPG-T-005, TPG-T-006, TPG-T-007, TPG-T-010, TPG-T-013, and TPG-T-014 already map cleanly to existing deterministic test assets.
Medium effort: TPG-T-002 requires extending the existing public relay harness to emit and record accepted OK responses without weakening event-driven semantics.
Medium effort: TPG-T-005 requires adding a signer/auth mock that lacks browser-visible NIP-44 support so the fail-closed path is proven without relying only on missing-discovery cases.
Completed: TPG-T-008 now uses an encrypted payment-history relay harness in `web/tests/e2e/dashboard-smoke.spec.js` and explicitly fails if the dashboard regresses to REST `payments/history`.
Medium effort: TPG-T-009 can likely be implemented as a static dependency/contract test over approved browser modules rather than a browser-run test.
High effort: TPG-T-012 depends on implementing or surfacing a service-authored NIP-51 kind 30002 relay-list path for the settings UI, consistent with HITL-SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP-004.
High effort: TPG-T-015 needs a combined Playwright harness that preserves one authenticated session while tracing both public and encrypted relay traffic separately.
TPG-T-011 is manual today because it checks classification across docs and approval evidence; if 311xx regressions recur, replace it with a doc-lint or proof-lint job.
